defects.description: The sports GTD fail-closed change in gtd() (kernel.py:356-359) is not behind a flag. With the default STRATEGIES it is unreachable because check() rejects sports modes first (0 decision differences), but a kernel built with a custom strategy table that trades sports modes now rejects makers that the audited Phase 1 kernel approved (my probe: 'within caps' became 'GTD: sports maker needs the market's start'). It is stricter only, and it closes the Phase 1 audit's wiring-later item, but it departs from the letter of ground rule 1.
defects.fix_hint: Accept and record it as an intentional fail-closed tightening, or gate it on the 'sports' flag.

defects.description: flag_notes tell WW-D that 'the worker calls kernel.clock(...)', following the Phase 2 note about a 60 s worker thread. RiskKernel.trip does a read-modify-write on scopes (kernel.py:174) with no lock. If the clock thread trips REDUCING while the main thread trips HALTED on the same scope, the two writes can interleave and leave REDUCING, downgrading the HALT.
defects.fix_hint: Have the worker only measure and the main tick call kernel.clock(), or put a threading.Lock around trip()/reset(). Tell WW-D either way.

defects.description: Phase 3 wiring items are only partly done, all failing closed and disclosed. defects.fix_hint: Track for the negRisk executor and live-risk follow-ups. No action needed while negrisk_scan is logging-only.
